prompt: A sales user can open an Account but cannot see its Margin field. Another user with the same profile can see it. What should you inspect first?
choices: Permission sets and permission set groups granting field access
The Account team's access level for the affected record
The profile's assigned Account page layout before considering permission sets
The user's territory membership and Account access
explanation: Field-level security can be extended through permission sets. Record sharing does not grant field access; page layouts alone are not a security boundary.

prompt: Opportunity OWD is Private. A specialist needs ongoing access to selected deals without receiving access to all deals in a region. Which feature best fits?
choices: Opportunity teams with appropriate record access
A criteria-based sharing rule covering every deal in the specialist's region
A role directly above all owners of the selected deals
View All on Opportunity paired with a filtered list view
explanation: Opportunity teams grant record-specific collaboration access without widening baseline access across unrelated opportunities.

prompt: A custom object has Private OWD. Managers must not inherit access through the role hierarchy. What should an administrator configure?
choices: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies for that custom object
Disable hierarchy inheritance on the managers' roles only
Replace Private OWD with Public Read Only and a restriction rule
Remove managers from the public groups used by sharing rules
explanation: Custom objects can disable hierarchy-based access. The same switch is not available for standard objects.

prompt: A user can edit an Account but cannot edit its Annual Revenue field even after it is added to the layout. What is the next check?
choices: Field-level edit permission and any other edit restrictions
The Account's sharing rule granting Read Only access
The Account owner's role relative to the user
The layout's section visibility before checking field permissions
explanation: Record edit access does not imply field edit access. A layout cannot override read-only field-level security.

prompt: A permission set group grants Delete through one component. One team should receive the group without that permission. What supports this requirement?
choices: A muting permission set in the group, provided no other source grants Delete
A restrictive sharing rule denying Delete to that team
A second permission set explicitly setting Delete to denied
Removing Delete from the profile while leaving all group grants intact
explanation: Muting removes selected grants from that group only. A separate profile or permission set can still grant the permission.

prompt: A contractor needs access to ten Accounts for two weeks. The records do not share a reliable attribute. What minimizes broad access?
choices: Manual sharing or Account team access to those records, followed by removal
A criteria-based rule using Account owner as a temporary proxy
A dedicated role above the ten Account owners
An Account list view shared with the contractor
explanation: Targeted sharing meets a limited record requirement. Time-bound cleanup must be planned; broad administrative permissions are unnecessary.

prompt: A user receives record access through a sharing rule and a manual share. You delete the manual share. Why does access remain?
choices: Sharing grants are additive; the rule still grants access
The user retains access until the record owner changes
Manual sharing removal requires a full sharing recalculation before taking effect
The rule cannot grant access unless a manual share also exists
explanation: Removing one access path does not remove access granted by another path. Inspect all effective grants.

prompt: An integration should read one custom object and update two fields, with no administrative access. What is the best design?
choices: A dedicated integration identity with minimum object and field permissions
A dedicated user with Modify All on the object and layout restrictions
A shared integration identity used by every external system
An employee identity with a permission set limited to the integration's fields
explanation: A dedicated least-privilege identity separates auditability and lifecycle from individual employees. UI layouts do not constrain API access.

prompt: A user can access a record through a list view but cannot find it in a different app's navigation. What is most likely?
choices: App navigation differs from record security
App assignment should be used to remove access to those records
Add the object to navigation to grant the missing object permission
Change OWD because list views provide an alternative sharing path
explanation: Navigation controls discoverability. Object, field, and record permissions determine access independently.

prompt: A confidential field must be hidden from users in reports, API responses, and record pages. Which control is required?
choices: Field-level security
A read-only field on all assigned page layouts
A custom report type excluding the field and a hidden Lightning component
A validation rule preventing nonadministrators from changing the field
explanation: Field-level security applies beyond a particular page. Layout and folder changes do not comprehensively protect the field.

prompt: Every Invoice Line must belong to an Invoice and inherit its owner and sharing. Invoice totals should summarize line amounts. Which relationship fits?
choices: Master-detail with a roll-up summary on Invoice
A required lookup with a formula summing all related line amounts
A lookup with inherited parent sharing enabled in the field settings
A master-detail relationship with Invoice Line as the master
explanation: Master-detail provides dependent ownership and sharing and supports native roll-up summaries on the master.

prompt: A custom child record must survive deletion of its related parent. The relationship must be optional. What should you use?
choices: A lookup with appropriate parent-deletion behavior
A master-detail relationship with cascade deletion disabled
A required lookup configured to prevent deletion of the parent
A master-detail relationship with reparenting enabled
explanation: An optional lookup can preserve independent child records. Confirm its deletion settings rather than assuming master-detail behavior.

prompt: Sales and Support need different picklist subsets and page layouts on the same object. What should you configure?
choices: Record types and assigned page layouts
Separate page layouts that independently define permitted picklist values
Permission sets assigning different picklist subsets directly
Record types alone, without reviewing layout and process assignments
explanation: Record types support process and picklist variations with layout assignment. They do not independently grant record access.

prompt: An administrator needs an Account field to show the current owner's department automatically. No historical snapshot is required. What fits?
choices: A cross-object formula where the relationship and field support it
A default-value formula on Account referencing the owner
A roll-up summary reading the owner's current department
A one-time before-save flow that copies the value only on Account creation
explanation: A formula reflects the referenced value dynamically. Defaults and copied values become stale without further updates.

prompt: A currency formula on Opportunity references the Account's risk category. A user lacks access to the source field. What risk must be evaluated?
choices: The formula may expose information derived from a field the user cannot view
The source field's permissions always prevent the formula from evaluating
Restricting the related object's tab guarantees the formula is safe
Making the formula read-only prevents disclosure of the source value
explanation: Cross-object formulas can surface derived information. Protect the formula itself and assess sensitive data exposure.

prompt: A business wants a field required for API imports as well as interactive edits. Which approach best enforces a conditional requirement?
choices: A validation rule evaluating the business condition
Mark the field required on each interactive page layout
Add a screen flow that checks the field before users save
Use a default value so API clients never need to supply the field
explanation: Validation rules enforce conditions during saves, including API operations, subject to explicitly designed exceptions.

prompt: An administrator changes a picklist label but integrations depend on the API value. What should be preserved?
choices: The existing API value used by integrations
Change the API value with the label and let integrations match by display text
Preserve the label and change only the API value
Reorder the values so integrations continue using the same position
explanation: Labels and API values serve different purposes. Preserve stable integration values and test dependent automation.

prompt: Two objects need a many-to-many relationship with relationship-specific fields. What is the standard pattern?
choices: A junction object connecting the two objects
Two direct lookup fields without an association record
One master-detail relationship with a multi-select picklist for the other side
A roll-up summary on each object holding the related record IDs
explanation: A junction object models each association as a record, allowing attributes and relationship constraints.

prompt: Marketing qualifies a Lead that represents a new contact at an existing Account. What should happen during conversion?
choices: Select the existing Account and create or match the Contact as appropriate
Create a new Account, then merge it after every conversion
Convert into the existing Account but always create a new Contact
Update the Lead's Company field to the Account name to establish the relationship
explanation: Lead conversion can associate records with existing Accounts and Contacts. Matching and duplicate policies should be considered.

prompt: Managers need the stages available to differ between new-business and renewal Opportunities. What is needed?
choices: Sales processes combined with Opportunity record types
Opportunity record types with page layouts, without separate sales processes
Separate page layouts that hide unwanted Stage values
A validation rule as the sole mechanism for providing different available stage lists
explanation: Sales processes select Opportunity stages; record types connect the process to the appropriate user experience.

prompt: A sales team must capture negotiated product quantities and prices on each deal. What should be configured?
choices: Products, price books, and Opportunity products
Products and price books without adding line items to Opportunities
A custom quantity field on Opportunity for each active product
Quotes alone, without configuring products or price book entries
explanation: Opportunity products connect products and price book entries to a deal with quantities and negotiated pricing.

prompt: A Campaign must distinguish Invited, Attended, and No Show while tracking responses. What should you configure?
choices: Campaign member statuses and which statuses count as responded
Lead status values synchronized to Campaign member status
One Campaign record type for each participation status
A formula on Campaign that derives responses from Lead conversion
explanation: Campaign member statuses represent participation and include response designation. They are distinct from Lead status.

prompt: A Lead assignment rule is configured, but imported Leads still belong to the importing user. What should you inspect?
choices: Whether the import method invokes the active assignment rule
Whether the importing user's role is above the intended queue members
Whether the rule criteria match the final owner rather than Lead fields
Whether the destination queue has access to the related Campaign
explanation: Assignment rule execution depends on the operation and applicable options. Merely configuring a rule does not force every save to invoke it.

prompt: An Opportunity's stage has changed but the forecast view does not match expectations. Which mapping should you review?
choices: The stage's forecast category and forecast configuration
The Opportunity probability without reviewing forecast categories
The owner's role alone, because stage mappings never affect forecasts
The Opportunity record type's page layout assignment
explanation: Opportunity stages map to forecast categories, and forecast configuration determines which information is included.

prompt: A sales manager wants a unified view of each salesperson's pipeline, with drill-down to deals. What is the best starting point?
choices: An Opportunity report grouped by owner and stage with a dashboard
A dashboard with manually entered pipeline totals per salesperson
An Account report grouped by owner, using Account annual revenue as pipeline
An Opportunity list view without grouping or aggregate reporting
explanation: An appropriately secured Opportunity report and dashboard support pipeline aggregation and record-level investigation.

prompt: Cases need to route to different queues based on product and severity when submitted. Which feature is the first fit?
choices: Case assignment rules with ordered criteria
Case escalation rules with a zero-hour threshold for every new Case
Case auto-response rules that assign the destination queue
A support process that maps every status directly to an owner
explanation: Assignment rules route incoming Cases. Escalation rules address elapsed-time conditions after intake.

prompt: Urgent Cases must notify management if unresolved after a defined business-hours interval. What should you configure?
choices: Case escalation rules using the appropriate business hours
Case assignment rules with an age-based formula as the only mechanism
Auto-response rules using a delayed email template
An entitlement process without reviewing whether simple escalation rules meet the need
explanation: Escalation rules evaluate age and criteria and can reassign or notify, with business hours affecting timing.

prompt: Customers should receive different acknowledgments depending on the submitted Case type. What feature fits?
choices: Case auto-response rules
A single organization-wide email signature for all Case submissions
Case assignment rule entries with an email template but no response rules
Case escalation rules that send the initial acknowledgment on creation
explanation: Auto-response rules send template-based acknowledgments based on criteria. Routing and escalation solve different needs.

prompt: Agents need consistent guided steps to gather information and create a Case while on a call. What should be considered?
choices: A screen flow exposed in the service experience
An autolaunched flow containing screen elements
A record-triggered flow that prompts the agent during the transaction
A validation rule guiding the agent through a sequence of dependent inputs
explanation: Screen flows support guided input and record actions. Before-save flows do not present screens.

prompt: Only approved support articles should be available to external readers. What must be evaluated together?
choices: Knowledge publication state, channel visibility, and audience access
Publication state alone, because published articles are visible to all audiences
Data categories alone, without channel or user access checks
Report folder access and Knowledge record ownership only
explanation: Publishing alone does not establish the intended audience. Channel and access configuration determine exposure.

prompt: A nightly import must update existing customer records and insert new ones without relying on Salesforce IDs. What should be used?
choices: Upsert using a properly governed external ID
Update by Account name after sorting the CSV
Insert using an external ID field without using an upsert operation
Upsert using a customer identifier that is allowed to repeat across source systems
explanation: Upsert uses the external ID to identify existing records. Uniqueness and source identity governance prevent ambiguous matches.

prompt: An import may create Accounts with names similar to existing customers. The business wants warnings or blocks based on matching criteria. What is required?
choices: Matching rules together with duplicate rules
A matching rule alone, without an active duplicate rule
A duplicate rule without defining or selecting matching logic
A unique text field using only the customer's displayed name
explanation: Matching rules identify possible matches; duplicate rules decide what happens when those matches are found.

prompt: A large update succeeds for some rows and fails validation for others. What is the safest next step?
choices: Review success and error outputs and retry only corrected failures
Retry the full file using Insert after removing the error column
Disable the failing rules and rerun every row without reconciliation
Assume the whole batch rolled back and repeat all operations
explanation: Partial results require reconciliation. Retrying only failures avoids duplicate creation or unintended repeated side effects.

prompt: Before bulk-changing record owners, what should an administrator do?
choices: Export relevant IDs and current owners and assess sharing and automation impacts
Export record names and new owner names without IDs
Change owners first and use a report afterward to reconstruct prior access
Disable sharing rules during the transfer and restore them without testing
explanation: Ownership can affect sharing, teams, and automation. Stable IDs and a pre-change snapshot support recovery.

prompt: A team wants to restore records after accidental deletion. What should be checked first?
choices: Recycle Bin availability and the scope and limits of undelete
Whether a recent data export can be imported directly without relationship reconciliation
Whether re-creating records with matching names preserves their original IDs
Whether the current report can recover deleted field values automatically
explanation: Recycle Bin recovery is time- and capability-limited. Assess related records and retain an independent backup strategy.

prompt: A required relationship must be populated during a migration. What sequence reduces failures?
choices: Load parent records, obtain their IDs or external IDs, then load children
Load children first using parent names, then deduplicate the parents
Load both objects independently and populate required relationships afterward
Use new Salesforce IDs from a different org as parent references
explanation: Parent references must resolve when children are loaded. An explicit mapping or supported external-ID relationship avoids name ambiguity.

prompt: A team assumes weekly CSV exports include every file and all metadata needed for full recovery. What should the admin explain?
choices: Backup coverage and restore procedures must be verified separately for data, files, and metadata
A successful export job proves a complete restore is possible
Metadata recovery is covered whenever all standard objects are exported
Recycle Bin retention is sufficient for long-term data and configuration recovery
explanation: A recoverable backup needs defined coverage and tested restore procedures; tabular data alone is not a complete org backup.

prompt: A user can open a report folder but sees fewer records than an administrator in the same report. Why?
choices: Report results respect the user's object and record access
The report folder's Viewer access restricts each user to a fixed row count
A report's creator always determines the data shown to every viewer
The report type automatically hides rows owned by other roles
explanation: Folder access permits access to the report asset; it does not override underlying data permissions.

prompt: Executives must see dashboard results according to each viewer's own access. Which approach fits?
choices: A dynamic dashboard, within org feature and limit availability
A fixed running-user dashboard owned by a broadly privileged executive
A public dashboard folder with an administrator as running user
A report filter set to My Records under a shared administrative running user
explanation: Dynamic dashboards run as the viewing user. A fixed privileged running user can expose broader aggregate results.

prompt: A report needs Accounts even when no related Opportunities exist. What should the report type support?
choices: Accounts with or without Opportunities
Accounts with Opportunities and a filter for blank Opportunity names
An Opportunity report with an outer filter on Account fields
Accounts with Opportunities and cross-filter logic that restores missing parents
explanation: The relationship definition in the report type controls whether parents without child records are included.

prompt: A manager wants each region's share of the report's grand total. Which tool is most appropriate?
choices: A summary formula using a parent grouping total
A row-level formula dividing each amount by a hard-coded total
A report bucket that calculates regional percentages automatically
A cross-object formula referencing the report's grand total
explanation: Summary formulas operate on grouped aggregates and can compare them to parent or grand totals.

prompt: A report filter uses AND for all conditions, but the requirement is West region OR strategic Accounts, limited to active customers. What should you configure?
choices: Custom filter logic combining the alternative criteria inside the active-customer requirement
Set all three conditions to OR so no strategic Account is excluded
Use West AND strategic AND active to enforce all three criteria
Put the active filter inside only the West branch of the OR expression
explanation: Explicit filter logic expresses grouped Boolean conditions; test boundary cases to avoid unintended inclusion.

prompt: A dashboard chart shows stale figures after records change. What should be checked before changing security?
choices: Dashboard refresh status and underlying report filters
The source report's folder access before checking whether the dashboard is cached
The running user's role alone, because dashboards always show live data
The dashboard component title, which determines its refresh frequency
explanation: Dashboards can display cached results. Refresh behavior and source report selection must be checked before concluding access is wrong.

prompt: A field on the triggering record should be populated efficiently before it is saved. No related records need updates. Which flow fits?
choices: A before-save record-triggered flow
An after-save flow that saves the same record again for every update
A scheduled-triggered flow that recalculates all records each hour
A formula field even when a stored, editable snapshot value is required
explanation: Before-save flows efficiently change fields on the triggering record without a second DML update.

prompt: After an Opportunity closes, a related Account must be updated and a Task created. Which flow timing is appropriate?
choices: An after-save record-triggered flow
A before-save flow that creates a Task through an immediate record action
A formula on Account referencing the triggering Opportunity's closed status
A scheduled flow that scans every Opportunity after each save
explanation: Actions involving related records or additional records require after-save processing rather than the fast field-update path.

prompt: A record-triggered flow updates a field and keeps re-entering automation on later saves. What should be examined first?
choices: Entry conditions, prior values, and whether updates actually need to occur
Increase the flow's trigger order so recursion is automatically prevented
Move the same unguarded update to an asynchronous path
Change every entry condition to always run so state stays synchronized
explanation: Precise transition checks and idempotent updates avoid repeated or recursive work. The design must consider the wider automation chain.

prompt: A bulk import hits limits because a flow queries and updates records inside a loop. What is the best correction?
choices: Collect IDs and records, then query and perform DML outside the loop
Move only the update outside the loop and keep a query per record
Split the flow into a subflow called once per loop iteration
Move the same per-record operations into an asynchronous path without redesign
explanation: Bulk-safe automation minimizes repeated database operations. Permissions do not raise transaction governor limits.

prompt: An approval process locks a submitted expense. A user can view it but cannot edit it. What should be investigated?
choices: Approval locking behavior and who may edit locked records
The record's page layout read-only settings as the only possible cause
The user's sharing rule, because approval locks do not affect edit access
The approval entry criteria alone, without checking the current approval state
explanation: Approval locks impose an edit constraint distinct from visibility. Review allowed editors and the process state.

prompt: An external system occasionally rejects a flow's action. Operations need a useful diagnostic and a controlled recovery route. What should be designed?
choices: Fault paths, safe error logging, and an appropriate retry or escalation process
Retry every failed action immediately without tracking completed operations
Write full request headers and credentials into a public error record
Suppress the failure and let the scheduled job repeat all actions later
explanation: Fault handling preserves context without exposing secrets. Retries must be bounded and account for duplicate side effects.

prompt: An administrator debugs a flow successfully as an admin, but users receive access errors. What is the next investigation?
choices: The flow's execution context and users' effective permissions
Grant users administrative permissions to match the successful debug run
Change the flow owner without examining execution context
Move the flow to a different Lightning page to bypass record access errors
explanation: Flow behavior depends on context and permissions. An administrator's successful run does not establish least-privilege user readiness.

prompt: A scheduled action should occur several days before a renewal date, but that date can change. What needs validation?
choices: Scheduled-path timing, updated dates, and entry/eligibility behavior
Whether the original schedule should remain unchanged after any renewal-date update
Only whether the flow was active when the record was created
Only the invoking user's time zone, without eligibility or update tests
explanation: Date-relative automation must be tested for changes, cancellation, and eligibility, not only the first scheduled execution.

prompt: A team asks for a formula field to send an email when a balance exceeds a limit. What should you recommend?
choices: Use appropriate automation; formulas calculate values and do not send emails
A formula with an email-template return type
A roll-up summary that invokes an email alert on evaluation
A required email field with a calculated default as the notification mechanism
explanation: Formulas compute values. Sending notifications requires an action through automation with clear triggering conditions.

prompt: Users need key fields and actions tailored to a mobile record header. What configuration should be reviewed?
choices: Compact layouts and supported mobile actions
Only the full page layout, because compact layouts apply exclusively to desktop
A Lightning record page assignment without checking mobile action support
A global action layout as the only control over all record highlights
explanation: Compact layouts influence record highlights, and supported actions determine mobile interactions. Test the actual mobile experience.

prompt: A Lightning component should appear only when a record is high priority. Which feature is appropriate?
choices: Component visibility filters on the Lightning record page
A separate record type for every priority value without visibility filters
A dynamic dashboard filtered to high-priority records
A page layout assignment that changes automatically whenever priority changes
explanation: Visibility filters tailor presentation to conditions. They are not a substitute for securing sensitive data.

prompt: Different apps require different Lightning record pages for the same object. What should be configured?
choices: Lightning page activation and relevant app, record type, and profile assignments
Page layout assignments alone, without Lightning page activation
A single org-default page with no app-specific activation
Separate profiles alone, because app activation cannot affect record pages
explanation: Activation assignments determine which record page appears in a given app and user context.

prompt: An admin hides a field using Dynamic Forms visibility. A user still retrieves it through the API. Why?
choices: Presentation visibility does not replace field-level security
Dynamic Forms filters require a new sharing calculation before they affect APIs
The API uses page layout visibility instead of field-level security
A record type assignment will enforce the same condition on API responses
explanation: Conditional UI visibility is presentation logic. Field-level security must enforce data confidentiality.

prompt: A team wants reusable email text while preserving personalization. What should be considered?
choices: Email templates with appropriate merge fields and access
Copy a prior customer email and manually replace names for every recipient
Use one fixed email body with no merge context to eliminate permission concerns
Grant all users access to every template folder to ensure personalization works
explanation: Templates support consistency and merge data. Validate merge context and access before broad use.

prompt: A new automation works in a sandbox. What is the strongest next step before production deployment?
choices: Test representative personas, bulk operations, negative paths, and deployment dependencies
Test a single successful record as admin and deploy using identical settings
Deploy only the flow without checking referenced fields or permissions
Perform bulk testing only after activation in production
explanation: Production readiness requires realistic permissions, transaction volumes, failure behavior, and dependency coverage.

prompt: A request would grant all support staff Modify All Data to resolve one access issue. What should the administrator do first?
choices: Diagnose object, field, and record access and apply the narrowest sufficient grant
Grant Modify All on the object before diagnosing the missing access layer
Place support above every record owner in the role hierarchy
Make the object Public Read Write and hide sensitive fields in layouts
explanation: Resolve the actual access layer. Broad administrative permissions bypass controls far beyond a single business requirement.

prompt: A release changes a standard feature used in critical automation. What is the best preparation?
choices: Review official release notes and test affected workflows in an appropriate preview or sandbox environment
Read release notes without testing the org's affected automation
Test only custom code because standard flows are insulated from release changes
Wait for production failures before reviewing the feature's new behavior
explanation: Release readiness connects documented changes with regression tests of actual dependencies.
